title: Xanadu and GlobalFoundries Partner to Scale Photonic Quantum Chip Production
source_used: Quantum Zeitgeist (rewrite of the companies' press release)
key_facts: Xanadu Quantum Technologies and GlobalFoundries (GF) will make components for utility-scale quantum computers on GF's 300 mm production line in Malta, New York
First priority is industrializing Xanadu's superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs)
These are to be combined with Xanadu's ultra-low-loss silicon nitride photonics, the backbone of its architecture
Companies say the detectors should speed up Xanadu's machines and cut chip overhead for large systems
They are also exploring high-performance quantum modules
Output is meant to underpin Xanadu's upcoming fault-tolerant demonstrators and future quantum data centers
No volumes, dates or financial terms given in the text read
quote_evidence: Transitioning quantum computing technology to a high-volume manufacturing line is fundamental to delivering quantum computing at scale, said Xanadu CEO Christian Weedbrook.
This partnership creates a path to industrialize the critical components needed to accelerate the deployment of fault-tolerant systems, said GF's Nicholas Sergeant.
why_it_matters_hint: Moves a photonic quantum design from lab prototypes toward factory production, but no volumes or dates are given.
notes: HPCwire original blocked (HTTP 403 Cloudflare); text read at Quantum Zeitgeist, which cites the companies' GlobeNewswire release. Barron's and Yahoo Finance report a share-price jump but were not read.
